Test whether the cardinality between time granules is fixed

Source: R/01_chronon_cardinality.R
chronon_cardinality_is_fixed.Rd

Tests whether the number of x time granules in a y time granule is a constant (e.g. 12 months in a year, 24 hours in a day), or instead depends on where in time it is measured (e.g. 28 to 31 days in a month, 52 or 53 weeks in a year). A fixed cardinality can be found with chronon_cardinality() alone, while an irregular one also needs a time point at.

Usage

chronon_cardinality_is_fixed(x, y)

Arguments

x

The finer time granule (e.g. cal_gregorian$month(1L))

y

The coarser time granule (e.g. cal_gregorian$year(1L))

Value

A single logical value.

Details

The cardinality is fixed when the granules are of the same time unit, or are connected only by chronon_cardinality_fixed() relationships. Granules with no relationship between them don't have a fixed cardinality.

Examples

# There are always 12 months in a year
with(cal_gregorian, chronon_cardinality_is_fixed(month(1L), year(1L)))
#> [1] TRUE

# The number of days in a month varies
with(cal_gregorian, chronon_cardinality_is_fixed(day(1L), month(1L)))
#> [1] FALSE

# The order of the granules doesn't matter
with(cal_gregorian, chronon_cardinality_is_fixed(day(1L), hour(1L)))
#> [1] TRUE
